query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: For face-centred-cubic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) that contain ≥12 at.% Cr, the dominant control parameter for resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion (tribocorrosion) is the time-averaged ratio τ = k_repass ⁄ k_remove, where k_repass is the electrochemical rate at which a compact Cr- (and, when present, Al-) rich nanocrystalline oxide film re-forms on freshly exposed surfaces, and k_remove is the mechanical rate at which sliding contact removes that film. Because sluggish diffusion and severe lattice distortion shorten cation diffusion paths while raising hardness, HEAs in which τ > 1 continuously maintain the protective tribofilm and exhibit markedly lower material loss than alloys with τ < 1.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution-annealed, cold-polished equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy discs (grain size 10–20 µm, fully FCC).
generation.intervention: Add 0.3 molar fraction Al to create Al0.3CoCrFeNi (maintains single-phase FCC + nanoscale L1_2 clusters) and repeat identical surface preparation.
generation.conditions: Reciprocating ball-on-disc test in naturally aerated 3.5 wt % NaCl at 25 °C, normal load 5 N, stroke length 5 mm, sliding speed 0.1 m s⁻¹, 3600 s total, potential held at open-circuit.
generation.structural_mediator: During sliding, a 50–150 nm thick mixed Cr/Al-rich (spinel + Cr2O3) tribofilm forms; its integrity and self-healing kinetics mediate the observed response.
generation.mechanism: High configurational entropy and lattice distortion in the Al-containing HEA (1) slow long-range diffusion so that freshly exposed metal quickly saturates in Cr and Al at the interface, (2) accelerate short-range cation transport required for oxide nucleation, and (3) raise near-surface hardness, decreasing k_remove. Together these effects raise τ above unity, letting the film persist and suppress both electrochemical dissolution and third-body abrasion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the Cr-only CoCrFeNi: (a) total material loss rate (wear + corrosion) of Al0.3CoCrFeNi will be lower by 50–70 %; (b) purely mechanical wear volume (from post-test profilometry after Faradaic correction) will drop by 40–60 %; (c) average corrosion current density integrated during sliding will fall by 30–50 %. 316L stainless steel tested in the same cell will show the highest loss, establishing an external baseline.
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNi without Al and conventional 316L stainless steel under identical test parameters.
generation.boundary: Prediction should hold in near-neutral chloride electrolytes (0.1–5 wt % NaCl), temperatures 20–80 °C, and normal loads ≤10 N. It may fail in strongly acidic media (pH < 1), in non-oxidising anhydrous conditions, or at sliding velocities ≥0.5 m s⁻¹ where k_remove overwhelms k_repass.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: quantitative values of k_repass for different HEA chemistries are scarce, and microstructural differences introduced during processing could mask the hypothesised effect.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three discs—CoCrFeNi, Al0.3CoCrFeNi, and 316L—under identical mechanical polishing and solution anneals. Perform tribocorrosion tests as specified. Continuously record (i) normal and friction forces, (ii) sliding potential and current (potentiostat, three-electrode setup), (iii) temperature. After testing, measure wear scars by 3D white-light interferometry, calculate mechanical wear volume, compute corrosion charge (Faraday’s law) to obtain purely electrochemical loss, and characterise the scar surface/ cross-section by TEM-EDS and XPS depth profiling for oxide thickness and composition.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Al0.3CoCrFeNi does NOT show (i) a ≥20 % thicker, chemically stable Cr/Al-rich tribofilm AND (ii) a statistically significant (>10 %) reduction in either wear volume or corrosion current compared with CoCrFeNi under the same conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
